strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing real industry need of identifying safety-critical scenarios from massive fleet data

High-quality dataset with 10,000 diverse queries, 10Hz annotations (higher than prior benchmarks), thoughtful verification procedure mixing procedural generation and manual annotation, and inclusion of negative examples

Clear novel task formulation that distinguishes scenario mining from related tasks (RMOT, VQA, motion planning) with specific requirements for object existence, 3D localization, and multi-agent reasoning
Comprehensive empirical analysis including multiple baselines, ground-truth oracles, failure case analysis, and ablation studies on LLM choice and temporal resolution
Practical methodology combining off-the-shelf perception with LLM-based program synthesis without requiring end-to-end training
Detailed reproducibility information with implementation details, API listings, and promised code/data release
weaknesses: Low absolute performance of all methods (50.1% HOTA-Temporal best case with GT tracks, 50.1% with predicted Le3DE2E tracks) raises serious questions about practical utility and validates concerns about approach limitations
Proposed RefProg method relies on hand-crafted 28 atomic functions making it unscalable; API fails on weather/lighting conditions; limited evidence of generalization beyond Argoverse 2

Dataset relatively small for long-term benchmark (1,000 logs) with limited annotations (no traffic lights, weather/lighting only in val/test); 79% procedurally generated scenarios may not capture real edge cases; no inter-annotator agreement reported

Missing critical experimental comparisons: no end-to-end learning baselines despite framing as zero-shot; unfair VLM baseline (RefInflate fails due to architectural mismatch not capability); no simpler alternatives like dense retrieval

Methodological concerns including ad-hoc hyperparameters (50% threshold, 1.5s dilation), inconsistent use of GT tracks (dataset generation) vs predicted tracks (RefProg), and unjustified implementation choices (DBSCAN parameters, confidence thresholds)

Incomplete analysis: no breakdown by scenario difficulty/category, missing runtime numbers despite 'prohibitively slow' claim, no human performance baseline, unclear impact of track quality on performance, no analysis of why standard HOTA degrades dramatically in RefProg predictions
Limited technical novelty: applies existing LLM program synthesis approach to new task; dataset contribution is solid but relatively incremental for a benchmark paper

Scalability and practical concerns: method limited to 50m range, urban only environments, fixed 15-20s clips; no evidence this formulation outcompetes simpler alternatives or helps actual AV development

strengths: Well-motivated and clearly articulated problem formulation distinct from RMOT/VQA
Higher temporal resolution (10Hz) enables capturing dynamic multi-agent interactions
Transparent methodology with pragmatic combination of procedural generation and manual verification
Comprehensive baseline comparisons providing useful context
Extensive implementation details and API listings in appendices
Inclusion of negative examples enables evaluation of false positives
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: RefProg is straightforward application of existing program synthesis techniques (VisProg/ViperGPT) with minimal algorithmic innovation
Weak empirical results: ~50% accuracy even with oracle tracks; large gap between oracle (64.8) and best real tracker (50.1) indicates extreme brittleness to perception noise
Fundamental architectural limitation: Method only filters pre-computed tracks and performs zero perception, so quality is hard-capped by upstream 3D detection accuracy

Critical scalability and practicality issues explicitly acknowledged as unresolved: prohibitively slow runtime, not suitable for real-world deployment, API design not scalable beyond hand-crafted 28 functions

Dataset quality concerns: Limited by AV2 annotation jitter; only 1.2% manually annotated (120/10K), majority procedurally generated by LLM; procedural generation error modes (relationship reversal, underspecified code) quantification missing
Small dataset scale: 10K prompts is modest relative to contemporaneous work (nuScenes: 2.2M, OmniDrive: 200K); unclear how LLM generation affects diversity
Severely restricted evaluation scope: 50m range limit, specific weather/lighting conditions, systematic spatial bias toward front of ego-vehicle (Fig. 7)
Limited failure analysis: All three baselines acknowledged to have unique failure modes but analysis is superficial with no quantification by scenario type or qualitative case studies
Incomplete ablations: No ablation on API design, confidence thresholds, or temporal dilation parameters; LLM robustness (0.5-2.9% failure rate variance) not thoroughly studied
RefBlind baseline surprisingly competitive (21.4 vs 50.1 HOTA-Temporal), raising questions about task difficulty and whether complex method is justified
Evaluation metrics not well justified (HOTA-Temporal/HOTA-Track distinction unclear); balanced accuracy may mask poor practical utility in imbalanced setting
Missing comparisons to recent multimodal VLMs (GPT-4V) that might better understand scenes; no rule-based baseline or database query approach included
No statistical significance testing, confidence intervals, or error bars provided
Design choices appear arbitrary (50m clipping, confidence filtering thresholds, 1.5s temporal dilation) without ablation or justification

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing genuine AV validation challenge; clear distinction from related tasks (RMOT, VQA, motion planning)
High-quality dataset with thoughtful curation combining LLM procedural generation and manual verification; 10Hz annotations enable fine-grained temporal reasoning
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with ground-truth oracles, failure mode analysis, and systematic ablations demonstrating RefProg's effectiveness
Thorough reproducibility support including complete API listing, implementation details, and promised code/data release
Clear empirical finding that off-the-shelf VLMs struggle with spatio-temporal scenario mining, motivating the program synthesis approach
Diverse annotations including negative prompts, weather, and lighting conditions; good dataset documentation in appendices
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty; RefProg is straightforward application of existing program synthesis ideas (VisProg, ViperGPT) without significant algorithmic innovation
Scalability concerns acknowledged but unresolved; authors explicitly state approach is 'not sufficiently efficient for real-world applications'; only evaluated on 1,000 logs
Hand-crafted API of 28 atomic functions is brittle and domain-specific; RefProg fails when API cannot express scenario (e.g., weather/lighting), contradicting compositional claims
Dataset scope limited to 1,000 Argoverse 2 logs with ~79% procedurally generated and only ~1.2% manually annotated; AV2 not designed for scenario mining
Ground-truth oracle achieves only 64.8 HOTA-Temporal but performance ceiling is not analyzed; no human evaluation of whether identified scenarios are safety-critical
Heavy coupling to perception quality; significant post-processing required (confidence filtering, timestamp dilation, downsampling); no analysis of quality degradation
Missing error analysis by scenario type; no qualitative failure cases shown; large tracker variance (9.4 HOTA-Temporal spread) unexplained
Zero-shot evaluation only; no cross-dataset generalization tested; unclear if results transfer to nuScenes, Waymo, or other domains

strengths: Clear problem formulation distinguishing scenario mining from RMOT/VQA with important insight that referred objects may not exist in logs
High-quality, well-designed dataset with 10,000 queries across 1,000 logs combining procedural generation and 200 hours of human verification
Rich annotations including weather, lighting, multi-agent interactions, and negative examples (2,090) enabling proper detection evaluation
Higher temporal resolution (10Hz vs 2Hz) enabling fine-grained motion understanding relative to prior work
Comprehensive experimental validation with multiple baselines, ablations, zero-shot generalization to nuPrompt outperforming trained methods
Strong reproducibility with detailed implementation, full API listing, and promised code/dataset release
Community challenge demonstrating practical utility and engagement
weaknesses: RefProg method shows limited technical novelty—straightforward application of existing program synthesis (VisProg/ViperGPT) to temporal domain without significant algorithmic innovation
Scalability concerns: RefProg requires hand-crafted API (28 functions), authors acknowledge approach is 'not scalable', fails on weather/lighting prompts outside API scope
Post-processing includes filtering by referred class, suggesting core method is incomplete and requires substantial engineering
Large performance gap to oracle (HOTA-Temporal: 64.8 vs 50.1 best method) and minimal challenge improvements (53.4 vs 50.1 baseline, only 3.3%) question practical significance
Dataset scale modest (1,000 logs) with 407 unique expressions compressed into 10,000 queries showing repetition; procedural generation only 70% successful
Temporal evaluation underutilizes 10Hz advantage: HOTA-Track metric ignores temporal mislocation, results downsampled to 2Hz in evaluation (Appendix F)
Experimental design: balanced accuracy on imbalanced data (79% positive) instead of F1/AUPRC; no trained end-to-end RMOT methods or diverse VLM baselines
Limited analysis: only 3 failure cases shown, no performance breakdown by scenario complexity/rarity, missing inter-annotator agreement for manual annotations
Critical details relegated to appendices (e.g., 10Hz advantage negated by downsampling), presentation could better highlight core contributions

strengths: Well-motivated practical problem: scenario mining from driving logs is important for AV safety validation
Rigorous dataset curation combining LLM-based procedural generation with 200 hours of manual verification and clear documentation of error modes
Higher temporal resolution (10Hz vs 2Hz) enabling finer-grained motion understanding compared to nuScenes
Comprehensive experimental design with multiple evaluation metrics, ablations, and cross-dataset evaluation on nuPrompt
Includes negative prompts unlike most prior RMOT/VQA datasets, allowing balanced accuracy measurement
Clearly distinguishes task (spatio-temporal scenario mining) from related tasks (RMOT, VQA)
Reproducibility emphasis with detailed appendices and promised code/dataset release
weaknesses: Dataset scale is limited: 10,000 queries is small compared to recent benchmarks (nuGrounding: 2.2M, nuScenes-QA: 460k). Only 120 manually annotated scenarios; 8,880 procedurally generated
Significant dataset quality gaps: no inter-annotator agreement, label noise estimates, or ground truth track quality metrics reported; 30% procedural generation failure rate unaddressed
Restrictive 50m range limitation due to perception model constraints severely limits applicability to real autonomous driving
Method (RefProg) lacks novelty: LLM-based code generation from APIs is well-established (VisProg, ViperGPT). Hand-crafted atomic functions per domain limit scalability

Evaluation limitations: small test set (150 logs) without confidence intervals or significance testing; suspicious oracle baseline (13.3% HOTA-Temporal); unfair nuPrompt comparison conflates tracker effects
Weak baselines: simple methods (CLIP, class filtering) are strawmen; no comparison to fine-tuned RMOT or modern multimodal LLMs; Filter-by-Class surprisingly strong but unexplained
Questionable claims: nuPrompt 'state-of-the-art' uses different tracker; connection to motion planning underdeveloped; modest competition improvements (53.4% vs 50.1%) suggest hyperparameter tuning
Limited failure analysis: only 3 error examples; no systematic study of hard scenario types or impact of tracking quality on performance
Presentation issues: 28-page appendix with key details hidden; late introduction of referred/related/other object distinction; Figure 1 caption excessive
Missing ablations on atomic function design, API sensitivity, and dataset bias (Argoverse 2 front-heavy referred object distribution acknowledged but not remedied)

strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation clearly articulating why scenario mining differs from RMOT, VQA, and motion planning
High-quality dataset construction combining LLM procedural generation with 200 hours of manual verification; 10Hz Argoverse 2 annotations enable fine-grained temporal reasoning
Comprehensive empirical evaluation with five baselines, detailed failure mode analysis, and ablation studies demonstrating systematic methodology
Strong generalization: RefProg achieves state-of-the-art on nuPrompt without dataset-specific modifications, validating atomic function design
Thorough reproducibility with detailed implementation (Appendix A-J), full API listing, promised code/data release, and clear prompts
Community engagement through challenge competition revealing advances (global context-aware generation, fault-tolerant code generation, batch prompting)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: program synthesis is established; RefProg is primarily an application to temporal domain with straightforward LLM-code-execution pipeline
Scalability concerns: hand-crafted atomic function API acknowledged by authors as 'not scalable'; fails on weather/lighting scenarios despite manual annotation support
Dataset constraints: only 1,000 logs from single source with unclear geographic/temporal coverage; 50m range clipping limits far-field scenarios; 30% procedural generation failure rate
Evaluation design issues: HOTA-Temporal metric only penalizes referred timestamps which may not require true compositional reasoning; no human evaluation; challenge winner beats baseline by only 3.3%

Unfair baseline comparisons: RefProg leverages structured API with pre-computed ground-truth tracks while ReferGPT/CLIP baselines operate on raw features; all methods are zero-shot without trainable alternatives

Missing critical analysis: no breakdown of errors by scenario type, no difficulty metrics, no ablation on temporal dilation post-processing, program failure rates vary 0.5%-18.1% by LLM suggesting brittleness

Generalization limitations: nuPrompt evaluation required removing HD map functions; unclear why AV2-designed atomic functions transfer; no analysis of performance degradation with different sensors/geographic regions
